does: Soaks dried tarhana in cold liquid and whisks it smooth, then whisks it into the pot and simmers it, stirring, until it thickens into a smooth, sour soup.

intro.what: Cooking tarhana soaks the dried mix cold, then simmers it to thicken a soup.
intro.why: It teaches why a starchy thickener is mixed cold before it meets heat.

how: Stir the tarhana into some of the cold liquid and leave it to soften.
Whisk it until it is smooth and free of lumps.
Whisk it into the pot of liquid before it boils, so that it thickens evenly.
Bring it up to a gentle simmer, stirring often, because it catches on the bottom.
Simmer until it is smooth and coats a spoon, and loosen it with hot liquid if it grows too thick.

cues.text: A smooth, even soup that coats the back of a spoon, with no lumps.
A pleasant sour smell, like yogurt and tomato.

mistakes.mistake: Dropping dry tarhana into hot liquid, so that it forms lumps that do not soften.
mistakes.fix: Soak it in cold liquid and whisk it smooth first.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving it to simmer unstirred, so that it catches and burns on the bottom.

quiz.question: Why soak tarhana in cold liquid first?
choices: So it softens and whisks smooth without lumps.
quiz.because: In hot liquid the outside sets before the inside softens, and lumps form.

quiz.question: What must you do while it simmers?
choices: Stir it often so it does not catch.
quiz.because: Tarhana thickens and catches on the bottom of the pot.

quiz.question: When is the soup ready?
choices: When it is thin and watery.
When it is smooth and coats a spoon.
quiz.because: A smooth soup that coats a spoon is fully thickened.

quiz.question: The soup is lumpy. What should change next time?
choices: Soak and whisk the tarhana cold first.
Add it dry to boiling liquid.
quiz.because: Cold soaking and whisking prevents lumps.
